title: Amplification of a Randomized Decision Procedure
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean lists, let $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $\delta,\varepsilon$ be positive rational numbers. Suppose $N$ uses space at most $s(|x|)$ on every input $x$ and every choice word. Suppose also that for each input $x$ there is a time bound $T$ such that every choice word of length $T$ halts; if $x \in L$, the probability of output $[\mathrm{true}]$ at time $T$ is at least $\delta$; and if $x \notin L$, every choice word of length $T$ produces output $[\mathrm{false}]$. Then there are a natural number $a$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N'$ over the Boolean alphabet that uses space at most $a s(|x|)$ on every input and choice word, and such that for each input $x$ there is a time bound $T$ at which every choice word halts, the probability of output $[\mathrm{true}]$ is at least $1-\varepsilon$ when $x \in L$, and every choice word produces output $[\mathrm{false}]$ when $x \notin L$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$L$ is a language of Boolean lists
$s$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers

On members of $L$, the acceptance probability at that bound is at least $\delta$
On nonmembers of $L$, every choice word at that bound outputs exactly $[\mathrm{false}]$
